indication: ** 55-year-old female presenting with left arm edema. Evaluate for thrombosis or venous compression.
technique: ** Helical CT imaging of the chest was performed following the administration of intravenous contrast. Multiplanar reformats were reviewed.
findings:
**
The lungs are clear without evidence of focal consolidation, pleural effusion, or pneumothorax. There is no suspicious pulmonary nodule identified. The tracheobronchial tree is patent.
Regarding the mediastinum, there is extensive filling defect noted within the left brachiocephalic vein, consistent with an extensive thrombus extending from its confluence with the internal jugular and subclavian veins toward the superior vena cava. There is associated upstream venous congestion with prominent collateral vessels visualized in the left chest wall and axillary region. No extrinsic compression of the vein by adjacent lymph nodes or masses is seen. The superior vena cava remains patent.
The heart size is within normal limits. No pericardial effusion is present. The thoracic aorta and great vessels follow a normal course.
Incidental findings include mild atherosclerotic calcifications along the descending thoracic aorta. There are small, benign-appearing calcified granulomas in the right lower lobe. The visualized upper abdominal organs are unremarkable. The bony structures show mild degenerative changes of the thoracic spine.
conclusion:
**
Extensive thrombus involving the left brachiocephalic vein with associated upstream venous congestion. No evidence of external venous compression.
